description: Two-tier pattern system: Tier 1 for symptom-based triage (discrimination), Tier 2 for root-cause confirmation and remediation

patterns.name: 503/5xx Service Errors
patterns.description: Triage pattern for 5xx HTTP errors. Discriminates between connectivity issues, routing problems, and cascading failures.

discriminating_queries.name: check_service_endpoints
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[:IN_NAMESPACE]->(ns:Namespace {name: $namespace}) OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[:SELECTS_PODS]->(p:Pod) RETURN s.name, count(p) as endpoint_count

discriminating_queries.name: check_downstream_failures
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[c:FAILED_CALL_TO]->(downstream:Service) WHERE c.status_code =~ '5..' RETURN downstream.name, c.status_code, c.last_observed ORDER BY c.last_observed DESC LIMIT 5

discriminating_queries.name: check_istio_routing
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (vs:VirtualService)-[:ROUTES_TRAFFIC_FOR]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) OPTIONAL MATCH (dr:DestinationRule)-[:DEFINES_POLICY_FOR]->(s) RETURN vs.name, vs.http_routes, dr.subsets

initial_investigation_steps: Check if the failing service has endpoints (SELECTS_PODS edges)
Check for FAILED_CALL_TO relationships to downstream services
For Istio environments: Check VirtualService and DestinationRule configuration
Determine if this is a network-layer (no response) or application-layer (error response) issue

patterns.name: 404 Not Found Errors
patterns.description: Triage pattern for 404 errors. Discriminates between missing routes, incorrect path matching, and missing services.

discriminating_queries.name: check_httproute_exists
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (hr:HTTPRoute)-[:ROUTES_TO]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN hr.name, hr.hostnames, hr.matches

discriminating_queries.name: check_service_exists
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[:IN_NAMESPACE]->(ns:Namespace {name: $namespace}) RETURN s.name, s.ports

discriminating_queries.name: check_virtualservice
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (vs:VirtualService)-[:ROUTES_TRAFFIC_FOR]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN vs.name, vs.http_routes

initial_investigation_steps: Check if HTTPRoute or VirtualService exists for the requested path
Verify the target Service exists and has the expected name
Check path matching rules (exact, prefix, regex)
Verify Gateway listener configuration matches the route

patterns.name: 429 Rate Limited
patterns.description: Triage pattern for rate limiting. Discriminates between single-caller overload and shared dependency bottleneck.

discriminating_queries.name: check_callers_to_target
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (caller:Service)-[c:FAILED_CALL_TO]->(target:Service {name: $service_name}) WHERE c.status_code = '429' RETURN caller.name, c.last_observed, c.error_count ORDER BY c.last_observed DESC

discriminating_queries.name: aggregate_by_target
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (caller:Service)-[c:FAILED_CALL_TO]->(target:Service) WHERE c.status_code = '429' WITH target, collect(caller.name) as callers, count(caller) as caller_count WHERE caller_count > 1 RETURN target.name, callers, caller_count ORDER BY caller_count DESC

initial_investigation_steps: Identify which service is returning 429s
Count how many different callers are seeing 429s from the same target
If multiple callers to same target: shared bottleneck (fan-in pattern)
Check target service capacity and current load

patterns.name: 401/403 Authentication Errors
patterns.description: Triage pattern for authentication/authorization failures. Discriminates between credential issues and permission problems.

discriminating_queries.name: check_shared_secrets
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_SECRET]->(s:Secret) WHERE p.name CONTAINS $service_name RETURN s.name, s.namespace, s.updated_at, collect(p.name) as affected_pods

discriminating_queries.name: check_multiple_services_affected
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Secret)<-[:USES_SECRET]-(p:Pod) WHERE s.name = $secret_name RETURN p.name, p.namespace, p.restart_count ORDER BY p.restart_count DESC

initial_investigation_steps: Identify which services are seeing auth failures
Check if multiple services are failing auth simultaneously
Query USES_SECRET edges to find shared credentials
Check Secret updated_at timestamps for recent changes
Correlate auth failure start time with Secret update time

patterns.name: Pod Crashes and Restarts
patterns.description: Triage pattern for pod failures. Discriminates between resource exhaustion, configuration errors, and image issues.

discriminating_queries.name: check_oom
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod {name: $pod_name}) RETURN p.status, p.restart_reason, p.memory_limit, p.memory_usage

discriminating_queries.name: check_image_pull
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod {name: $pod_name}) RETURN p.status, p.image, p.events

discriminating_queries.name: check_configmap_usage
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_CONFIG]->(cm:ConfigMap) WHERE p.name = $pod_name RETURN cm.name, cm.updated_at

discriminating_queries.name: check_deployment_rollout
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (d:Deployment)-[:MANAGES]->(rs:ReplicaSet)-[:MANAGES]->(p:Pod) WHERE p.name = $pod_name RETURN d.name, rs.name, rs.desired_replicas, rs.current_replicas, p.status ORDER BY rs.created_at DESC

initial_investigation_steps: Check Pod events for specific error messages (OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, etc.)
If OOMKilled: investigate memory usage and limits
If ImagePullBackOff: check image name and pull credentials
If CrashLoopBackOff: check for recent ConfigMap/Secret changes
Check if this is part of a Deployment rollout (multiple ReplicaSets)

patterns.name: Multi-Service Simultaneous Failures
patterns.description: Triage pattern when multiple unrelated services fail at once. Discriminates between shared infrastructure, shared config, and shared dependency.

discriminating_queries.name: check_shared_node
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:SCHEDULED_ON]->(n:Node) WHERE p.name IN $pod_names WITH n, collect(p.name) as pods, count(p) as pod_count WHERE pod_count > 1 RETURN n.name, pods, pod_count, n.status ORDER BY pod_count DESC

discriminating_queries.name: check_shared_configmap
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_CONFIG]->(cm:ConfigMap) WHERE p.name IN $pod_names WITH cm, collect(p.name) as pods, count(p) as pod_count WHERE pod_count > 1 RETURN cm.name, cm.updated_at, pods, pod_count ORDER BY pod_count DESC

discriminating_queries.name: check_shared_dependency
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (caller:Service)-[c:FAILED_CALL_TO]->(target:Service) WITH target, collect(caller.name) as callers, count(caller) as caller_count WHERE caller_count > 2 RETURN target.name, callers, caller_count ORDER BY caller_count DESC

discriminating_queries.name: check_node_events
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (e:K8sEvent)-[:INVOLVES]->(n:Node) WHERE e.reason IN ['NodeNotReady', 'Draining', 'DiskPressure', 'MemoryPressure', 'EvictionThresholdMet'] RETURN n.name, e.reason, e.message, e.last_timestamp ORDER BY e.last_timestamp DESC LIMIT 10

initial_investigation_steps: Identify all affected pods/services
Check if pods share a common Node (SCHEDULED_ON)
Check if pods share a common ConfigMap (USES_CONFIG)
Check if services call a common failing dependency (FAILED_CALL_TO)
Check K8sEvents for Node-level issues (drain, pressure, eviction)

patterns.name: High Latency
patterns.description: Triage pattern for latency issues. Discriminates between local service issues and dependency chain problems.

discriminating_queries.name: check_downstream_latency
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[c:CALLS]->(downstream:Service) RETURN downstream.name, c.avg_latency_ms, c.p99_latency_ms ORDER BY c.p99_latency_ms DESC

discriminating_queries.name: check_pod_resources
discriminating_queries.query: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[:SELECTS_PODS]->(p:Pod) RETURN p.name, p.cpu_usage, p.cpu_limit, p.memory_usage, p.memory_limit

initial_investigation_steps: Identify which service is slow
Check CALLS relationships to downstream services for latency data
Check pod resource utilization (CPU/memory pressure)
If downstream is slow, traverse the dependency chain to find the bottleneck
For trace data: aggregate span durations by service to find slowest

patterns.name: Service Selector Mismatch
patterns.description: Service exists, pods exist and are Running, but Service selector doesn't match Pod labels resulting in zero endpoints.
investigation_steps: Query Service selector: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN s.selector
Query pods in same namespace: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:IN_NAMESPACE]->(ns:Namespace {name: $namespace}) WHERE p.name CONTAINS $service_name RETURN p.name, p.labels
Compare Service.selector with Pod.labels to find mismatch
Check if there was a recent Deployment update that changed labels
Verify SELECTS_PODS edge count is 0
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: The Service selector must exactly match Pod labels for endpoints to be created. Common causes: label typos, version label mismatches after rollout, copy-paste errors. The Service works but has no backends to send traffic to.
recommendations: Fix Service selector to match Pod labels
Or update Deployment template to include missing labels
Verify endpoints appear after fix: kubectl get endpoints $service_name
Add label validation to CI/CD pipeline
Consider using label selectors without version for stable service discovery

patterns.name: Cascading Failure
patterns.description: A leaf service failure propagates upstream through the dependency chain, causing multiple services to fail. The alerted service is a symptom, not the root cause.
investigation_steps: Start at alerted service, query downstream: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[c:CALLS|FAILED_CALL_TO]->(downstream:Service) WHERE c.status_code =~ '5..' RETURN downstream.name, c.status_code
Follow the chain recursively (depth-first) until finding a service with no failing downstream calls
The leaf service (no downstream failures) is the root cause
Verify leaf service status and check its specific issue
Assess blast radius by counting affected upstream services
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Errors cascade UPSTREAM. Follow calls DOWNSTREAM to find root cause. The service that is failing but has NO failing dependencies is the origin. Check timestamps: which service failed first? Leaf services typically show application errors, not 'downstream unavailable' messages.
recommendations: Fix the root cause issue in the leaf service first
Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascade amplification
Add timeout and retry policies with exponential backoff
Implement graceful degradation for non-critical dependencies
Add health checks and readiness probes
Document service dependencies and criticality levels

patterns.name: Pod Resource Exhaustion
patterns.description: Pod is being killed or throttled due to exceeding resource limits or node-level resource pressure.
investigation_steps: Check Pod events: MATCH (p:Pod {name: $pod_name}) RETURN p.status, p.restart_reason, p.restart_count
Spawn metrics investigation for memory and CPU trends
Compare actual usage against requests and limits
Check if limits are too restrictive or if there's a memory leak
For OOMKilled: check memory_usage vs memory_limit at time of kill
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: OOMKilled means the container exceeded its memory limit. CPU throttling means it's hitting CPU limits. Distinguish between: 1) limits too low (increase them), 2) application bug causing excessive usage (fix the app), 3) unexpected load spike (scale out).
recommendations: Increase resource limits based on actual usage patterns
Identify and fix memory leaks or CPU-intensive operations
Scale horizontally with more replicas
Implement HPA for automatic scaling
Add resource monitoring and alerts for early detection

patterns.name: Configuration Error
patterns.description: Pod fails to start due to configuration issues: missing ConfigMap/Secret references, invalid volume mounts, or bad application config.
investigation_steps: Check Pod events for specific error messages
Verify ConfigMap and Secret references exist: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_CONFIG|USES_SECRET]->(ref) WHERE p.name = $pod_name RETURN ref.name, ref.namespace, labels(ref)
Check volume mount paths and permissions
Review application startup logs for configuration errors
Verify environment variable references are correct
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: CrashLoopBackOff with quick restarts usually indicates config issues. The container starts but fails validation or can't find required resources. Check Pod events first - Kubernetes often tells you exactly what's wrong.
recommendations: Fix missing or incorrect ConfigMap/Secret references
Correct volume mount paths or add missing volumes
Validate configuration syntax and required fields
Use init containers to validate configuration before main container starts
Add configuration validation to CI/CD pipeline

patterns.name: HTTPRoute Misconfiguration
patterns.description: HTTPRoute is missing, has incorrect path matching, or doesn't properly reference the backend Service.
investigation_steps: Check if HTTPRoute exists: MATCH (hr:HTTPRoute)-[:ROUTES_TO]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN hr.name, hr.hostnames, hr.matches
Verify path matching rules cover the requested paths
Check Gateway listener configuration matches HTTPRoute
Verify backend Service reference is correct
Check for conflicting routes with overlapping paths
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: 404 with no matching route means the Gateway can't find a path to the backend. Check the 'negative space' - what routes are MISSING that should exist? Path matching is order-sensitive and type-sensitive (exact vs prefix vs regex).
recommendations: Create HTTPRoute for the missing path
Fix path matching rules to cover required paths
Correct backend Service references
Fix Gateway listener configuration
Document route architecture and ownership

patterns.name: VirtualService Subset Mismatch
patterns.description: Istio VirtualService routes traffic to a subset that has no matching pods. The DestinationRule defines the subset labels, but no pods have those labels.
investigation_steps: Get VirtualService routing: MATCH (vs:VirtualService)-[:ROUTES_TRAFFIC_FOR]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN vs.name, vs.http_routes
Extract subset name from route destination
Get DestinationRule subset definition: MATCH (dr:DestinationRule)-[:DEFINES_POLICY_FOR]->(s:Service {name: $service_name}) RETURN dr.subsets
Count pods matching subset labels: MATCH (s:Service {name: $service_name})-[:SELECTS_PODS]->(p:Pod) WHERE p.labels CONTAINS $subset_label RETURN count(p)
If count is 0, the subset has no backing pods
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Envoy 'UH' (No healthy upstream) flag with Istio often means subset mismatch. Correlate 3 layers: VirtualService (which subset?) → DestinationRule (what labels?) → Pods (do any match?). This commonly happens after deployments when version labels change.
recommendations: Deploy pods with the required subset labels
Update VirtualService to route to an existing subset
Remove subset routing to use all available pods
Ensure Deployment labels match DestinationRule subset definitions
Add subset validation to deployment pipeline

patterns.name: Node Resource Contention
patterns.description: Multiple pods on the same node are degraded because one pod (noisy neighbor) is consuming excessive resources, causing contention.
investigation_steps: Find common node: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:SCHEDULED_ON]->(n:Node) WHERE p.name IN $affected_pod_names RETURN n.name, collect(p.name) as pods
Get all pods on that node: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:SCHEDULED_ON]->(n:Node {name: $node_name}) RETURN p.name, p.namespace, p.cpu_usage, p.cpu_limit, p.memory_usage ORDER BY p.cpu_usage DESC
Calculate total resource pressure: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:SCHEDULED_ON]->(n:Node {name: $node_name}) RETURN n.cpu_capacity, sum(p.cpu_request) as total_requested
Identify the outlier pod consuming most resources
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: When multiple unrelated services degrade simultaneously, check if they share infrastructure. The pod with highest resource usage relative to others is likely the noisy neighbor. Node-level metrics show overall pressure; pod-level metrics identify the culprit.
recommendations: Move the noisy neighbor pod to a different node (add anti-affinity rules)
Add resource limits to the noisy neighbor
Use pod priority and preemption for critical workloads
Implement pod disruption budgets
Consider dedicated nodes for resource-intensive workloads

patterns.name: ConfigMap Propagation
patterns.description: A ConfigMap update with bad values propagates to multiple pods, causing them to crash or malfunction after the config is mounted.
investigation_steps: Find shared ConfigMap: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_CONFIG]->(cm:ConfigMap) WHERE p.name IN $affected_pod_names WITH cm, collect(p.name) as pods RETURN cm.name, cm.namespace, cm.updated_at, pods
Check ConfigMap update timestamp vs pod crash times
Query all pods using that ConfigMap: MATCH (cm:ConfigMap {name: $configmap_name})<-[:USES_CONFIG]-(p:Pod) RETURN p.name, p.namespace, p.restart_count, p.last_restart_time
Check K8sEvents for ConfigMap changes
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: If multiple pods crash shortly after a ConfigMap update (within minutes), the new config values are likely invalid. ConfigMap propagation takes ~60 seconds for volume mounts. Correlation: if crash_time - configmap_updated_at < 5 minutes, likely related.
recommendations: Revert ConfigMap to previous known-good values
Add configuration validation before applying changes
Use staged rollouts for config changes (canary one service first)
Implement config change auditing
Add application-level config validation on startup

patterns.name: Diamond Dependency Bottleneck
patterns.description: Multiple unrelated services all depend on the same downstream service, which becomes a bottleneck. Fan-in pattern where the shared dependency is overloaded.
investigation_steps: Aggregate failures by TARGET: MATCH (caller:Service)-[c:FAILED_CALL_TO]->(target:Service) WHERE c.status_code IN ['429', '503'] WITH target, collect(caller.name) as callers, count(caller) as caller_count WHERE caller_count > 1 RETURN target.name, callers, caller_count ORDER BY caller_count DESC
Identify the bottleneck service (most callers with failures)
Check bottleneck service capacity: MATCH (s:Service {name: $bottleneck})-[:SELECTS_PODS]->(p:Pod) RETURN count(p) as replica_count, p.cpu_limit, p.memory_limit
Compare incoming request rate vs service capacity
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Key insight: aggregate by TARGET service, not SOURCE. If 3+ different services are all failing calls to the same target, that target is the bottleneck. The individual callers aren't broken - they're all hitting the same overloaded dependency.
recommendations: Scale the bottleneck service horizontally
Add caching layer in front of the bottleneck
Implement rate limiting per caller to ensure fair access
Add circuit breakers in callers to fail fast
Consider async patterns to reduce synchronous load

patterns.name: Shared PVC Exhaustion
patterns.description: Multiple pods mount the same PVC (ReadWriteMany). One pod fills the disk, causing write errors in all pods sharing that storage.
investigation_steps: Find shared PVC: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:MOUNTS]->(pvc:PersistentVolumeClaim) WHERE p.name IN $affected_pod_names WITH pvc, collect(p.name) as pods RETURN pvc.name, pvc.capacity, pods
Check PVC usage: MATCH (pvc:PersistentVolumeClaim {name: $pvc_name})-[:BOUND_TO]->(pv:PersistentVolume) RETURN pvc.capacity, pvc.used, pv.path
Find pod consuming most disk: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:MOUNTS]->(pvc:PersistentVolumeClaim {name: $pvc_name}) RETURN p.name, p.disk_usage ORDER BY p.disk_usage DESC
Identify which pod wrote the most data
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: HTTP 507 (Insufficient Storage) or gRPC ResourceExhausted with disk errors across multiple pods suggests shared storage exhaustion. The pod with highest disk_usage on the shared PVC is likely the culprit.
recommendations: Increase PVC capacity
Clean up old data from the volume
Add per-pod storage quotas
Implement log rotation and data retention policies
Consider separate PVCs for heavy writers

patterns.name: Deployment Rollout Stuck
patterns.description: Deployment rollout is stuck because new ReplicaSet pods can't start (usually ImagePullBackOff or CrashLoopBackOff), while old ReplicaSet keeps serving traffic.
investigation_steps: Get Deployment and ReplicaSets: MATCH (d:Deployment {name: $deployment_name})-[:MANAGES]->(rs:ReplicaSet) RETURN d.name, rs.name, rs.created_at, rs.desired_replicas, rs.current_replicas ORDER BY rs.created_at DESC

Compare old vs new ReplicaSet pod status: MATCH (d:Deployment {name: $deployment_name})-[:MANAGES]->(rs:ReplicaSet)-[:MANAGES]->(p:Pod) RETURN rs.name, rs.created_at, collect({pod: p.name, status: p.status, ready: p.ready}) as pods ORDER BY rs.created_at DESC
Check new ReplicaSet pods for specific errors
If ImagePullBackOff: verify image name and registry credentials
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Multiple ReplicaSets = rollout in progress. If the newer ReplicaSet has 0 ready pods while older one is healthy, the new version can't start. Check new RS pod status: ImagePullBackOff (bad image), CrashLoopBackOff (app issue), or Pending (scheduling issue).
recommendations: Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/$name
Fix image tag if ImagePullBackOff
Fix application if CrashLoopBackOff
Check image pull secrets if authentication issue
Add image validation to CI/CD pipeline

patterns.name: Secret Rotation Cascade
patterns.description: A Secret rotation with invalid credentials causes auth failures across all pods using that Secret. Multiple services fail auth simultaneously after the rotation.
investigation_steps: Find shared Secret: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:USES_SECRET]->(s:Secret) WHERE p.name IN $affected_pod_names WITH s, collect(p.name) as pods RETURN s.name, s.namespace, s.updated_at, pods
Check Secret update timestamp vs auth failure start time
Find all pods using that Secret: MATCH (s:Secret {name: $secret_name})<-[:USES_SECRET]-(p:Pod) RETURN p.name, p.namespace, p.restart_count
Verify if rollback is possible (previous Secret version)
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Multiple services failing 401/403 at the same time is a strong signal of credential rotation gone wrong. Check USES_SECRET edges to find the common Secret. If auth failures started within minutes of Secret update, correlation is strong.
recommendations: Rollback Secret to previous valid credentials
Validate credentials before applying rotation
Implement staged credential rotation (update one service first)
Use external secret management with validation
Add credential testing to rotation process

patterns.name: Node Drain Impact
patterns.description: A node is being drained or experiencing issues (DiskPressure, MemoryPressure), causing all pods on that node to be evicted and rescheduled.
investigation_steps: Find common node: MATCH (p:Pod)-[:SCHEDULED_ON]->(n:Node) WHERE p.restart_count > 0 WITH n, collect(p.name) as pods, count(p) as count WHERE count > 3 RETURN n.name, pods, count ORDER BY count DESC

Check node events: MATCH (e:K8sEvent)-[:INVOLVES]->(n:Node {name: $node_name}) WHERE e.reason IN ['NodeNotReady', 'Draining', 'DiskPressure', 'MemoryPressure', 'EvictionThresholdMet'] RETURN e.reason, e.message, e.last_timestamp ORDER BY e.last_timestamp DESC
Verify node status: MATCH (n:Node {name: $node_name}) RETURN n.status, n.conditions, n.taints
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: When multiple pods restart across different services but share a node, check for node-level events. Draining, DiskPressure, MemoryPressure all cause mass evictions. The node is the root cause, not the individual pods.
recommendations: Wait for drain to complete, pods will reschedule
Uncordon node if drain was unintended
Add node capacity if resource pressure
Ensure pod distribution with anti-affinity rules
Implement pod disruption budgets for critical workloads

patterns.name: NetworkPolicy Block
patterns.description: NetworkPolicy is blocking traffic between namespaces or services. Connection times out (not refused) because packets are dropped.
investigation_steps: Check if caller and target are in different namespaces: MATCH (caller:Service {name: $caller_service})-[:IN_NAMESPACE]->(callerNs:Namespace) MATCH (target:Service {name: $target_service})-[:IN_NAMESPACE]->(targetNs:Namespace) RETURN callerNs.name, targetNs.name
If different namespaces, check NetworkPolicies in target namespace
Verify target pods are healthy (to distinguish from other 503 causes)
Check if NetworkPolicy allows ingress from caller's namespace
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Connection TIMEOUT (not refused) with healthy target pods suggests NetworkPolicy blocking. If target returns 503/500, that's application error (network works). If connection times out and target is healthy, check NetworkPolicy. Cross-namespace calls are commonly blocked by default deny policies.
recommendations: Update NetworkPolicy to allow traffic from caller's namespace
Add appropriate labels to caller pods for NetworkPolicy matching
Document which namespaces are allowed to communicate
Consider namespace labels for simpler policy management
Test connectivity after NetworkPolicy changes
